basis: 14 of 25 tracked indices rose in their latest session.
VIX closed at 25.64 (-9.01% on the day).
Rule: Risk-on = 65%+ of indices up and VIX not rising; Risk-off = 35% or fewer up, or VIX up 8%+; otherwise Mixed.

headline.technical: Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% (1d) into correction territory as an AI-stock selloff spread to Asia and Europe; Nikkei 225 fell 5.96%, KOSPI 6.02%, and the VIX closed at 26.90.
headline.layman: AI and tech shares fell sharply in the US, then in Asia and Europe. India's market rose as investors looked for a way around AI stocks.

status.technical: The Financial Times reported the Wall Street AI sell-off spread to Asia and Europe; CNBC said the Nasdaq Composite entered correction territory. S&P 500 1d -4.36%, Nasdaq 1d -5.52%, VIX 5d 38.52%.
status.layman: AI-related shares fell hard in the US. CNBC says the Nasdaq entered a 'correction'. The fall then spread to Asia and Europe. The VIX, a gauge of market fear, jumped over the week.

consequence.technical: Bloomberg reported trend-following systematic funds amplified the plunge. If that selling fades, pressure may ease; historically after falls this size the S&P 500 next 5 days rose 58% of 153 times. Base rates are not predictions.
consequence.layman: Bloomberg says automatic, trend-following funds made the drop bigger. If they stop selling, pressure could ease. Past patterns are not forecasts.

impact.technical: CNBC reported Asian chip names SK Hynix, Samsung, Softbank and TSMC tumbled. The Financial Times said the sell-off is deep but not broad, yet. WSJ reported the DXY rose to a one-week high.
impact.layman: Chip and tech firms took the biggest hit. The Financial Times says the sell-off is deep but not yet broad. The US dollar held up well.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls above 1 standard deviation, the S&P 500 next day rose 47% of 154 times and next 5 days rose 58% of 153 times; the Nasdaq next 5 days rose 54% of 169 times.
outlook.layman: History only: after drops like this, the following week was up slightly more often than down. This is not a forecast.

regions.title: Americas: US tech rout, Mexico cuts

status.technical: Dow -3.44%, Nasdaq -5.52%, S&P 500 -4.36% (1d). Bloomberg reported Banxico unexpectedly cut to 6.25%; WSJ reported Brazil's central bank held rates after five consecutive cuts.
status.layman: US stocks fell hard. Mexico's central bank surprised by cutting its rate to 6.25%. Brazil's central bank paused after five cuts in a row.

consequence.technical: The Financial Times reported futures pointed to small gains at the opening bell; Investing.com reported Nasdaq futures rose as the AI rout paused amid dip buying. If that holds, selling may pause.
consequence.layman: Futures, which are bets on the market open, pointed to small gains. If that holds, the fall could pause for now.

impact.technical: Mexico's IPC rose 0.38% (1d) while Bovespa is -19.68% over 1m. The notes give no reason for Bovespa's slide, so evidence is thin.
impact.layman: Mexico's market rose a little. Brazil's has dropped a lot over the month, and the notes do not explain why.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: the S&P 500 next 5 days rose 58% of 153 times after comparable falls; the Dow next day rose 56% of 162 times.
outlook.layman: History only: after similar drops, US stocks were up a week later a bit more often than not. Not a forecast.

regions.title: Europe: lower on AI rout and energy-hit consumers

status.technical: FTSE 100 -2.19%, DAX -2.29%, CAC 40 -1.77%, Euro Stoxx 50 -1.58% (1d). Reuters said European shares were set to fall as the global AI rout gathered pace. WSJ reported eurozone retail sales fell as high energy prices weighed on confidence.
status.layman: European stocks fell with the global tech sell-off. WSJ says shoppers in the eurozone spent less because energy costs are high.

consequence.technical: The Financial Times reported the Stoxx Europe 600 is ahead of the S&P 500 this year. Yahoo Finance reported on Thursday that easing energy prices helped and the Bank of England raised rates. If energy keeps easing, support may hold.
consequence.layman: Europe is still doing better than the US this year, per the Financial Times. If energy costs keep easing, that could help.

impact.technical: Per the hand-kept lists, ASML +2.99% (1d) was the only riser among the largest Euro Stoxx 50 names; none of the largest DAX, CAC 40 or FTSE 100 names rose. WSJ cites energy costs weighing on consumers.
impact.layman: Almost all of Europe's biggest companies fell. Only chipmaker ASML rose. Households are feeling the high cost of energy.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls above 1 standard deviation, the DAX next 5 days rose 54% of 161 times, the FTSE 100 64% of 157 times and the Euro Stoxx 50 55% of 159 times.
outlook.layman: History only: after similar drops, European markets were up a week later more often than not. Not a forecast.

regions.title: Asia-Pacific: chip-heavy markets slump, India gains

status.technical: Nikkei 225 -5.96%, KOSPI -6.02%, TAIEX -4.51% (1d); Nifty 50 +2.01%, Sensex +2.17%. The Financial Times reported Japan's biggest one-day fall since 'liberation day' chaos; Bloomberg said Taiwan's benchmark entered bear-market territory.
status.layman: Japan, South Korea and Taiwan fell sharply, mostly on AI and chip stocks. India's market rose.

consequence.technical: Bloomberg reported Taiwan imposed a short-selling limit and authorized its stabilization fund; WSJ said Taiwan joined South Korea in moves to stem losses. If these steps calm trading, volatility may ease, but that is not assured.
consequence.layman: Taiwan and South Korea took steps to calm their markets. If they work, wild swings could ease, but nothing is guaranteed.

impact.technical: Mint reported AI and semiconductor stocks sold off in Nikkei 225, Kospi and Taiwan. Business Standard reported Indian equities headed for their biggest weekly gain in over five years amid the 'anti-AI' trade. SK Hynix -10.44%, Samsung Electronics -6.35% (1d).
impact.layman: Chip makers in Korea and Taiwan were hit hardest. Business Standard says investors favoured India as a way to avoid AI stocks.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after comparable falls KOSPI next 5 days rose 52% of 151 times, TAIEX 60% of 148 times and Nikkei 225 58% of 161 times.
outlook.layman: History only: after similar drops these markets rose a week later slightly more often than not. Not a forecast.

status.technical: Al Jazeera reported global markets were roiled by concerns over US data centre expansion and AI regulation. CNBC reported Equinix said smaller data centers may be less exposed to U.S. restrictions.
status.layman: Worries about new US limits on AI and data centres are shaking global markets.

consequence.technical: If US restrictions on data centres tighten, AI-infrastructure shares could stay under pressure; the notes do not say whether that will happen.
consequence.layman: If the US tightens rules, AI firms could stay under pressure. The notes do not say if that will happen.

impact.technical: Nvidia -9.26% (1d) and Broadcom -10.43% (1d) led the declines among the largest Nasdaq names; none of the eight rose.
impact.layman: The biggest AI chip companies fell the most.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: the Nasdaq next 5 days rose 54% of 169 times after comparable falls.
outlook.layman: History only, not a forecast: the week after similar falls was up slightly more often than down.

drivers.title: Oil falls as Iran risk is weighed

status.technical: CNBC reported oil prices fell Friday as investors weighed renewed Iran war escalation risk after the midterms against prospects for a diplomatic breakthrough. Brent 5d -16.37%, close 98.38.
status.layman: Oil prices fell this week as investors weighed the risk of more conflict with Iran against hopes for diplomacy.

consequence.technical: CNBC reported rate hikes could be curbed by an Iran war resolution, slower U.S. growth and fresh fiscal policy, but none are set in stone.
consequence.layman: If the Iran conflict is resolved, interest-rate rises could be held back, CNBC says, but none of this is certain.

impact.technical: The Economic Times reported the Indian rupee strengthened past 94/$ as oil slid and foreign inflows returned.
impact.layman: Cheaper oil helped the Indian rupee.

outlook.technical: Base rate, not a prediction: Brent next 5 days rose 51% of 846 times after ordinary days.
outlook.layman: History only: after ordinary days, oil was up a week later about half the time. Not a forecast.

status.technical: US 10-year yield closed at 4.84 (1d -1.16%). WSJ reported the DXY rose to a one-week high and ING expects it to trade toward the middle of a 101.500-102.500 range. WSJ reported Norway's central bank held and signalled readiness to tighten.
status.layman: US borrowing costs eased a little. The dollar held up. Norway's central bank signalled it may raise rates.

consequence.technical: CNBC reported the Democratic sweep gives markets a reason to rethink the path of interest rates. Analysts quoted by Business Standard said expectations of further Fed tightening could limit gold's upside.
consequence.layman: Markets are rethinking where interest rates go next. Some analysts still expect the Fed to raise rates.

impact.technical: WSJ argued the case for buying Treasury bonds is still strong as AI fears take down stocks and bonds offer compelling yields.
impact.layman: WSJ says bonds look attractive after the stock fall because they pay good interest.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls above 1 standard deviation the US 10-year yield next 5 days rose 56% of 154 times; the DXY next 5 days rose 52% of 187 times after big rises.
outlook.layman: History only: yields and the dollar were up a week later about half the time or a bit more. Not a forecast.

drivers.title: US midterms and the gold bid

status.technical: Mint reported the Democratic Party's sweeping victory triggered a sell-off in AI and semiconductor stocks. Bloomberg reported gold is set for its biggest weekly gain since August after the midterms; gold 5d 4.54%.
status.layman: Mint says the Democratic win in the US midterms set off the sell-off in AI stocks. Gold had its best week since August, per Bloomberg.

consequence.technical: Business Standard quoted an analyst saying gold's upside could stay constrained if expectations of further Fed tightening persist, particularly if US data stay firm or oil rebounds.
consequence.layman: One analyst says gold's gains may be limited if the Fed keeps raising rates.

impact.technical: WSJ reported the midterm shake-up matters for markets and investors; the notes give few details, so evidence is thin.
impact.layman: The notes say the election matters for investors but give few details.

outlook.technical: Base rate, not a prediction: gold next 5 days rose 56% of 853 times after ordinary days.
outlook.layman: History only: gold was up a week later slightly more often than not. Not a forecast.

events.layman: A US inflation report is due next week while tech shares are under pressure.

companyEffects.layman: Taiwan's biggest chip maker fell sharply, pulling its market lower.

companyEffects.technical: CNBC reported Softbank tumbled with Asian chip and tech stocks.
companyEffects.layman: SoftBank fell sharply with other tech names.

companyEffects.technical: Business Standard reported ICICI Bank extended its rally, up 10% in 4 days, with market cap near ₹11 trn.
companyEffects.layman: ICICI Bank kept rising and is now worth nearly ₹11 trillion.
